groups.theme: No acceptance criteria; a test without assertions would pass

suggestions.title: No acceptance criteria; a test without assertions would pass
suggestions.desc: The plan has no acceptance criteria. Its only testing requirement is to 'verify' three operand classes, which does not say the tests must assert the returned value. A test that calls add(1, 2) without comparing the result would pass even if add returned None or the wrong sum. The plan should state that each case asserts the exact expected sum, for example add(2, 3) == 5, add(-2, -3) == -5, add(0, 0) == 0 and a mixed-sign case.
suggestions.scope_reason: Makes the existing verification requirement checkable, with no new behaviour.
suggestions.scope_reference: Verify positive, negative and zero operands with unittest.

suggestions.title: No acceptance criterion for the verification step
suggestions.desc: The plan lists the operand classes to verify but gives no pass criterion. It does not say that all unittest cases must pass, or that add must return the exact sum for each class. It also does not say what counts as 'zero operands': both zero, or one zero and one non-zero. These cases can be read differently, so the implementer cannot tell when the work is done. The plan should state the acceptance condition, such as all cases pass with exact results, and enumerate the zero cases.
suggestions.scope_reason: Adds the pass condition for the testing the plan already requires.
suggestions.scope_reference: Plan line 3: 'Verify positive, negative and zero operands with unittest.'

suggestions.title: Operand types are not specified
suggestions.desc: The plan says add(a, b) returns a+b but does not say which operand types are supported (int only, floats, Decimal, Fraction, strings, mixed types) or what should happen for unsupported types (raise TypeError, return NotImplemented behaviour, or let Python's own error propagate). The tests it asks for cover only positive, negative and zero operands, so the type contract is untested and undefined. The plan should name the supported types and the expected error for others.
suggestions.scope_reason: Defining the input contract is needed to implement and verify the add function the plan already requires.
suggestions.scope_reference: Implement add(a, b) returning a+b in arithmetic.py

suggestions.title: Signature is only partly given; operand types are undefined
suggestions.desc: The plan names add(a, b) but gives no type expectations for a and b and no return type. 'Returning a+b' for ints gives an int, for floats a float, and for strings a concatenation, and the plan does not say which inputs are supported. It also does not say what happens for non-numeric inputs such as None or str, or whether bool is accepted. The 'preserve this public signature' requirement cannot be checked without this. The plan should state the supported types, the behaviour for unsupported types (raise TypeError, or pass through to Python's +), and whether mixed int/float is in scope.
suggestions.scope_reason: Defines the behaviour the plan already requires for add(a, b); it adds no capability.

groups.theme: Plan has no problem statement, objective or file list

suggestions.title: Plan has no problem statement, objective or file list
suggestions.desc: The plan is a single sentence and lacks the sections a design document needs: a problem statement or objective (why an add helper is needed in the project), the list of files changed and their purpose, and an explicit list of what is out of scope. Without the file list an implementer cannot tell whether anything besides arithmetic.py and a test module is expected, such as a package __init__ or a README entry.
suggestions.scope_reason: The baseline asks for a file list and objective, but does not say how much design detail is wanted for a plan this small.

suggestions.title: Plan lacks problem statement, objectives and file change list
suggestions.desc: The plan is a single sentence. It has no problem statement or objective (why add is needed, or what consumes it), no list of file changes (the new or changed arithmetic.py and a test file), and no description of the architecture or the stdlib-only constraint's scope. The plan is expected to contain these sections. Without the file list an implementer does not know whether to touch any file besides arithmetic.py, and the stdlib-only requirement is stated without saying what it covers (the implementation, the tests, or both).
suggestions.scope_reason: Fills in the plan sections the review expects; it does not add a feature.

groups.theme: Plan omits the public signature it says to preserve

suggestions.title: Plan omits the public signature it says to preserve
suggestions.desc: The plan says 'Preserve this public signature' but never states the signature. It only says 'Implement add(a, b) returning a+b'. An implementer cannot tell whether the parameters are positional-only, keyword-capable, or carry type hints or defaults, so 'preserve' has no defined target. The plan should state the exact signature, for example 'def add(a, b):' with its parameter names and any annotations.
suggestions.scope_reason: Stating the signature the plan already asks to preserve completes its existing requirement.
suggestions.scope_reference: Implement add(a, b) ... Preserve this public signature.

suggestions.title: Plan says preserve a signature, but no arithmetic.py exists
suggestions.desc: The plan says 'Preserve this public signature' for add(a, b) in arithmetic.py, which implies an existing module. The repository has no arithmetic.py and no other .py file (checked the repo root and find over the tree), so there is nothing to preserve. The implementer cannot tell whether to create the module or modify one elsewhere. The plan should state that arithmetic.py is new, or name the existing file and its current signature.
suggestions.scope_reason: Resolves the plan's own instruction about the file it asks to change; adds no new work.
suggestions.scope_reference: Plan line 3: 'Implement add(a, b) returning a+b in arithmetic.py ... Preserve this public signature.'

groups.theme: Test file location and run command are not specified

suggestions.title: Test file location and run command are not specified
suggestions.desc: The plan says to 'Verify positive, negative and zero operands with unittest', but it does not name the test file, its location, or how it is run (for example python -m unittest, or a discover pattern). Without that, the verification step has no defined target and nothing in the plan says the tests must be runnable from the repository root. The plan should give the test file path and the exact command.
suggestions.scope_reason: Specifies how the unittest verification the plan already asks for is run.
suggestions.scope_reference: Plan line 3: 'Verify positive, negative and zero operands with unittest.'

suggestions.title: Test file location and run method are not given
suggestions.desc: The plan asks to 'Verify positive, negative and zero operands with unittest' but names no test file, no test module path, and no command to run the tests. It also does not say whether arithmetic.py already exists. If it does, 'preserve' and 'implement' pull in different directions and the implementer must decide whether to overwrite it. The plan should name the test file path and the run command (for example python -m unittest) and state whether arithmetic.py is new or existing.
suggestions.scope_reason: Where the verification lives is part of the testing requirement the plan already states.
suggestions.scope_reference: Verify positive, negative and zero operands with unittest.
